[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Semillon_grapes_at_Ch%C3%A2teau_Doisy-V%C3%A9drines%2C_Barsac%2C_Sauternes.jpg/250px-Semillon_grapes_at_Ch%C3%A2teau_Doisy-V%C3%A9drines%2C_Barsac%2C_Sauternes.jpg)](/wiki/File:Semillon_grapes_at_Ch%C3%A2teau_Doisy-V%C3%A9drines,_Barsac,_Sauternes.jpg)

[Sémillon](/wiki/S%C3%A9millon "Sémillon") grapes in [Barsac](/wiki/Barsac_AOC "Barsac AOC")

White Bordeaux is predominantly, and exclusively in the case of the sweet [Sauternes](/wiki/Sauternes_(wine) "Sauternes (wine)"), made from [Sémillon](/wiki/S%C3%A9millon "Sémillon"), [Sauvignon blanc](/wiki/Sauvignon_blanc "Sauvignon blanc") and [Muscadelle](/wiki/Muscadelle "Muscadelle"). As with the reds, white Bordeaux wines are usually blends, most commonly of Sémillon and a smaller proportion of Sauvignon blanc. Typical blends are 80% Sémillon and 20% Sauvignon blanc. Other permitted grape varieties are [Sauvignon gris](/wiki/Sauvignon_gris "Sauvignon gris"), [Ugni blanc](/wiki/Ugni_blanc "Ugni blanc"), [Colombard](/wiki/Colombard "Colombard"), [Merlot blanc](/wiki/Merlot_blanc "Merlot blanc"), [Ondenc](/wiki/Ondenc "Ondenc") and [Mauzac](/wiki/Mauzac_(grape) "Mauzac (grape)"). Recently permitted by Bordeaux wineries, three new white grapes have been added: [Alvarinho](/wiki/Albari%C3%B1o "Albariño"), [Petit Manseng](/wiki/Petit_Manseng "Petit Manseng"), and Liliorila.[[15]](#cite_note-:0-15)

In the late 1960s Sémillon was the most planted grape in Bordeaux. Since then it has been in constant decline although it still is the most common of Bordeaux's white grapes. Sauvignon blanc's popularity on the other hand has been rising, overtaking Ugni blanc as the second most planted white Bordeaux grape in the late 1980s and now being grown in an area more than half the size of that of the lower yielding Sémillon.

**Sergio Mattarella** (Italian: [[ˈsɛrdʒo mattaˈrɛlla]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 23 July 1941) is an Italian politician who has been serving as the [president of Italy](/wiki/President_of_Italy "President of Italy") since 2015. He is the longest-serving president in the [history of the Italian Republic](/wiki/History_of_the_Italian_Republic "History of the Italian Republic"). Since [Giorgio Napolitano](/wiki/Giorgio_Napolitano "Giorgio Napolitano")'s death in 2023, Mattarella is the only living Italian president.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

A [Catholic leftist](/wiki/Catholic_left "Catholic left") politician, Mattarella was a leading member of the [Christian Democracy](/wiki/Christian_Democracy_(Italy) "Christian Democracy (Italy)") (DC) party from the early 1980s until its dissolution. He served as [Minister for Parliamentary Relations](/wiki/Italian_Minister_for_Parliamentary_Relations "Italian Minister for Parliamentary Relations") from 1987 to 1989, and [Minister of Education](/wiki/Italian_Minister_of_Education "Italian Minister of Education") from 1989 to 1990. In 1994, Mattarella was among the founders of the [Italian People's Party](/wiki/Italian_People%27s_Party_(1994) "Italian People's Party (1994)") (PPI), serving as the [Deputy Prime Minister of Italy](/wiki/Deputy_Prime_Minister_of_Italy "Deputy Prime Minister of Italy") from 1998 to 1999, and [Minister of Defence](/wiki/Minister_of_Defence_(Italy) "Minister of Defence (Italy)") from 1999 to 2001. He joined [The Daisy](/wiki/The_Daisy "The Daisy") (DL) in 2002 and was one of the founders of the [Democratic Party](/wiki/Democratic_Party_(Italy) "Democratic Party (Italy)") (PD) in 2007, leaving it when he retired from politics in 2008. He also served as a judge of the [Constitutional Court of Italy](/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Italy "Constitutional Court of Italy") from 2011 to 2015.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

[Marathi](/wiki/Marathi_language "Marathi language") is the most spoken language, spoken by about 35.4% of the population. [Hindi](/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") is the second–most-spoken language, spoken by 24.8% of the population, followed by [Urdu](/wiki/Urdu "Urdu") (11.7%) and [Gujarati](/wiki/Gujarati_language "Gujarati language") (11.4%).[[233]](#cite_note-census2011-langreport-236)[[235]](#cite_note-238)[[236]](#cite_note-51st_Report_CLMI-239) Marathi and English serve as the official languages of the government.[[236]](#cite_note-51st_Report_CLMI-239) English is the principal language of the city's [white collar](/wiki/White-collar_worker "White-collar worker") workforce. A colloquial form of Hindi, known as *[Bombay Hindi](/wiki/Bombay_Hindi "Bombay Hindi")* is spoken on the streets.[[237]](#cite_note-240) Many Hindi speakers are workers from [Uttar Pradesh](/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh") and [Bihar](/wiki/Bihar "Bihar") who migrate seasonally to Mumbai to work as labourers.[[238]](#cite_note-241)

Hurley in 2007

Hurley founded YouTube in 2005 with [Steve Chen](/wiki/Steve_Chen "Steve Chen") and [Jawed Karim](/wiki/Jawed_Karim "Jawed Karim"). On October 9, 2006, Chen and Hurley sold YouTube to [Google Inc.](/wiki/Google "Google") (now [Alphabet](/wiki/Alphabet_Inc. "Alphabet Inc.")) for $1.65 billion. It was reported in *[The Wall Street Journal](/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")* that Hurley's share was $345.6M at Google's February 7, 2007, closing stock price of $470.01. He received 694,087 Google shares directly and another 41,232 shares in a trust.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

YouTube's other two co-founders, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim, received 625,366 shares and 137,443 shares, respectively valued at $326.2M and $64.6M. The *Journal*'s report was based on Google's registration statement with [SEC](/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") filed on February 7, 2007.

Hurley resigned as CEO of YouTube in October 2010 but stated he would remain as an advisor of YouTube. [Salar Kamangar](/wiki/Salar_Kamangar "Salar Kamangar") was appointed to the CEO position following Hurley's resignation.[[12]](#cite_note-VatorNews-12)

War of the Third Coalition :: Prelude :: Setting up the opposing forces :: chunk_0006
When Napoleon crowned himself Emperor on December 2, 1804, Austria and Prussia may have been alarmed, but the annexed Italian city-states of Genoa, Parma and Piacenza and his coronation as King of Italy left no doubt as to Napoleon's intentions. On January 21, 1805, Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger presented a treaty of alliance with Russia and Austria. The demands of this treaty were the restoration of the Kingdom of Piedmont-Sardinia, the withdrawal of French troops from Italy, the dissolution of the Batavian Republic and the restoration of Switzerland's independence. In the event of Napoleon's refusal, England would support the coalition forces financially. After all difficulties had been resolved, the United Kingdom, Austria and Russia signed a treaty on August 9, 1805, forming the third coalition against Napoleon. Prussia remained neutral.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchneid200583–87-7)
On the other side, Napoleon built an alliance of various southern German members of the Holy Roman Empire. These included Württemberg, Bavaria and Baden, which benefited from the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of February 25, 1803. These enlarged states were in line with Napoleon's calculations. They were to weaken Austria, but were themselves too weak to pose a threat to France.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGotthard2003160-8)

The U.S. Supreme Court consists of nine members: one chief justice and eight associate justices. The U.S. Constitution does not specify the size of the Supreme Court, nor does it specify any specific positions for the court's members. The Constitution assumes the existence of the office of the chief justice, because it mentions in [Article I, Section 3, Clause 6](/wiki/Article_One_of_the_United_States_Constitution#Clause_6:_Trial_of_Impeachment "Article One of the United States Constitution") that "the Chief Justice" must preside over impeachment trials of the [President of the United States](/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"). The power to define the Supreme Court's size and membership has been assumed to belong to Congress, which initially established a six-member Supreme Court composed of a chief justice and five associate justices through the [Judiciary Act of 1789](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1789 "Judiciary Act of 1789").

The size of the court was first altered by the [Midnight Judges Act](/wiki/Midnight_Judges_Act "Midnight Judges Act") of 1801 which would have reduced the size of the court to five members upon its next vacancy (as federal judges have [life tenure](/wiki/Life_tenure "Life tenure")), but the [Judiciary Act of 1802](/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1802 "Judiciary Act of 1802") promptly negated the 1801 act, restoring the court's size to six members before any such vacancy occurred. As the nation's boundaries grew across the continent and as Supreme Court justices in those days had to [ride the circuit](/wiki/Circuit_riding "Circuit riding"), an arduous process requiring long travel on horseback or carriage over harsh terrain that resulted in months-long extended stays away from home, Congress added justices to correspond with the growth such that the number of seats for associate justices plus the chief justice became [seven in

The **Italian campaign** of [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), also called the **Liberation of Italy** following the [German occupation](/wiki/Operation_Achse "Operation Achse") in September 1943, consisted of [Allied](/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") and [Axis](/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") operations in and around [Italy](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy"), from 1943 to 1945. The joint [Allied Forces Headquarters](/wiki/Allied_Force_Headquarters "Allied Force Headquarters") (AFHQ) was operationally responsible for all Allied land forces in the [Mediterranean theatre](/wiki/Mediterranean_and_Middle_East_theatre_of_World_War_II "Mediterranean and Middle East theatre of World War II") and it planned and led the [invasion of Sicily](/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily "Allied invasion of Sicily") in July 1943, followed in September by the [invasion of the Italian mainland](/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Italy "Allied invasion of Italy") and the campaign in Italy until the [surrender](/wiki/Surrender_of_Caserta "Surrender of Caserta") of the [Axis forces](/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") in Italy in May 1945.

The invasion of Sicily in July 1943 led to the [collapse of the Fascist Italian regime](/wiki/Fall_of_the_Fascist_regime_in_Italy "Fall of the Fascist regime in Italy") and the fall of [Mussolini](/wiki/Mussolini "Mussolini"), who was deposed and arrested by order of King [Victor Emmanuel III](/wiki/Victor_Emmanuel_III_of_Italy "Victor Emmanuel III of Italy") on 25 July. The new government signed an [armistice with the Allies](/wiki/Armistice_of_Cassibile "Armistice of Cassibile") on 8 September 1943.
